blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh notified the Pedestrian Safety and Universal Accessibility Policy, 2026 on 7 August 2026 after cabinet approval on 6 August 2026. The policy combines pedestrian safety, universal design, and statutory accountability in a statewide framework for roads, footpaths, and public spaces.

items: Andhra Pradesh became the first state in India to notify an integrated statewide framework for pedestrian safety and universal accessibility.
The policy prioritises 15 to 20 high-fatality blackspots using historic accident data.
It mandates road-safety audits covering at least 20% of the state’s roads in the first year.
Article 21 of the Constitution of India protects the Right to Life and has been used in road safety jurisprudence.
